A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fairshare data-pricing work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix F report original LLM fine-tuning accuracy, acquisition costs, and simulated buyer utility, seller profit, and participation.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices E–F report these original experiments, with additional oracle-validation and discount-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The core pricing objectives and royalty extension remain. However, Appendix F.1 Algorithm 1 newly resets the supplied price p_j to zero before checking purchases; v1 checks the supplied price. This changes the printed procedure, although an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions specify MathQA and GSM8K for mathematics, MedQA for medical diagnosis, and PIQA for physical reasoning. The new oracle and discount-sensitivity analyses use retained tasks and market coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds DataInf to the valuation comparisons in Figures 6 and 9, and a one-step training oracle in Figure 8. The pricing comparator set remains unchanged: Current is renamed Exploitative and retains the same 10%-of-average-utility rule.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 changes the stated LoRA learning rate from 2e-7 to 2e-5. The default 100-step pricing simulation changes its discount factor from 0.999 to 0.98, alongside new multi-discount and one-step-oracle/Spearman evaluation protocols. These materially revise reported experimental settings without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond renaming the retained valuation experiment an ablation, v2 adds tests of InflIP–oracle agreement and downstream accuracy (Appendix F.2, Figure 8), plus discount-factor sensitivity of the fairshare crossover time (Appendix E.2, Figure 7). These introduce substantive checks of valuation approximation and pricing robustness absent from v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run/seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 checklist item 7 explicitly acknowledges this omission; the added correlations are point metrics, without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Fine-tuning accuracy/cost and market-welfare curves are revised under changed settings. For example, Llama/MathQA changes from InflIP leading in v1 Figure 3a to Constant leading in v2 Figure 6b. New results include oracle correlations of about 0.54 for MathQA and 0.42 for PIQA, and crossover times 32, 38, and 44 for discount factors 0.999, 0.99, and 0.98.

T1.justification: V2 adds a participation-loss bound (Lemma 6) and discount/crossover analysis (Lemma 7), revises the crossover definition, adds a nonnegative-part operation to MWP, and restricts the participation-sensitivity assumption's domain. Much of the earlier buyer-optimality proof is reused under the new failure lemma. Lemma 7 contains conflicting monotonicity statements.

C1.justification: The central fairshare, mutual-benefit, and performance-per-dollar claims remain. V2 adds an explicit main contribution claiming robustness across valuation methods and utility measures.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 newly explains how moderate valuation agreement can still yield similar downstream accuracy as purchased data increases. Appendix G.1 adds limitations concerning larger-scale and human-participant validation. Section 4.3 also strengthens the interpretation favoring InflIP's cost/performance balance, despite Constant remaining cheapest in Figure 6a.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly specifies single-A6000-GPU training taking less than one hour and revises the learning-rate disclosure. Appendix E.2 newly states that seller arrival order is shuffled each period. Both versions still promise future code release.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand positioning around exploitative data labor, AI parachuting, epistemic injustice, and dynamic participation. New citations include DataInf, GREATS, economic foundations, and additional data-market studies, while earlier TRAK/LOGIX and influence-method discussion is reduced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and theoretical exposition are extensively rewritten. V1 Sections 4–6 become v2 Section 4, with pricing preceding valuation; the impact statement moves to Appendix G. The title changes and a submission checklist is added.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format, adds the market diagram, combines old profit panels with new simulations in Figure 2, and adds Figures 7–8. Valuation plots gain DataInf and reordered panels; appendix tables and figures are relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The oracle and discount-sensitivity checks, explicit limitations, and compute details strengthen evidence and transparency. However, v1 correctly identifies Constant as cheapest, whereas v2 claims InflIP costs less despite Figure 6a; v2 also introduces conflicting statements in Lemma 7 and the price-reset discrepancy in Algorithm 1. These gains coexist with unresolved problems in interpretation, theory, and method documentation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
